item.title: A deep dive into Ivory Coast's solar energy goals
item.description: Can Ivory Coast, which remains heavily dependent on fossil fuels, turn to solar power to make its energy consumption greener and more sustainable? We visited the country's new solar power plant in Ferkessédougou, in the north of the country. Inaugurated in July, it is expected to generate nearly 90 gigawatt-hours of electricity a year. Report by Julia Guggenheim.

item.title: Why the Nvidia scandal is bad news for Europe’s AI ambitions
item.description: Nvidia's Jensen Huang poured money into open-source AI, from French-founded Hugging Face to chips for Mistral's data centres, and fought Washington's attempts to restrict it. With Huang gone and China hawks emboldened, Tech 24 asks whether Europe's AI ambitions have lost their most powerful ally, and whether he was ever the champion Europe needed.

item.title: US probes nationwide flights stoppage as travel disruptions persist
item.description: US air travel is expected to return to normal this Sunday, following a nationwide ground stop Friday night that stranded hundreds of thousands of passengers and disrupted travel worldwide. The Trump administration blamed the incident on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines and said there was no evidence this was a cyberattack. The ground stop now raises questions about the country's aging infrastructure and lawmakers are calling for an investigation. Analysis by Philip Mann, aviation expert at Vector Strategic Consulting.

item.title: Chinese spy, chip sales, Trump ties... The Nvidia scandal deepens
item.description: The Nvidia scandal continues to unravel. Sunday, the Singapore-based company Megaspeed said that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang had officially left the company in 2025. She is the alleged Chinese spy that had an affair with Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang. Late last year, revelations showed she was being investigated for chip smuggling. The scandal has also raised questions about how much the US government knew – Trump was allegedly warned about the affair but did not react. Analysis by Laïla Mörch, CEO of Shael and tech investor in Paris.

item.title: The week in pictures: Spain protests, Pope Leo's Peru 'homecoming' and Rocky fans in Philly
item.description: FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the week's most striking images, from angry protests over a housing crisis that has dominated Spain's election campaign, to Leo XIV's visit to his adopted homeland Peru and "Rocky" fans marking 50 years since the release of boxing movie classic.
